errorCodes.meaning: HCP `invalid-token` (HCP 5.5): "Missing, malformed, or expired authorization evidence", here the access token the request presents. A token issued under a revoked grant, a relinquished one included (HCP 5.2.7), fails here too: HCP requires that no request presenting evidence issued under a revoked grant succeeds, but names no error (HCP 6.2.2), and this family reads that evidence as invalid, pending HCP confirmation (question 2). Such a failure is itself a notice of revocation to the client (HCP 6.2.2). Defined once for the family in [the hcp family conventions](/specs/hcp/_shared/0.1/CONVENTIONS.md#1-family-error-codes).

Assertion.description: What the submitting client states about the assertion (HCP 4.2). `confidence` is REQUIRED and non-null when `declarationType` is `model-inferred`, and null or absent otherwise (HCP 4.2, 4.4). This rule is stated here and not as a schema conditional: the registry's Rust generator does not support `if`/`then`/`else`, so a validator does not check it.

basis.description: What the assertion was drawn from (HCP 4.2.5).

confidence.description: How confident an inferring model is (HCP 4.2, 4.4).

declarationType.description: What kind of party made the assertion (HCP 4.4); never omitted. HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

permittedPurposes.description: The purposes the asserter permits the entry to be used for; absent means no limit (HCP 4.2.6). The bound of 256 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

validUntil.description: The instant after which the content no longer holds; absent or null means it does not expire (HCP 4.2). Not the instant after which a disclosed copy stops being usable, which is a disclosure's `useUntil` (HCP 7.6).

Assurance.description: How a Context Asserter's identity was established (HCP 3.6). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

Basis.description: What an assertion was drawn from (HCP 4.2.5). It identifies no party but the Context Subject.

drawnFrom.description: The sources the assertion was drawn from. The bound of 256 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

rationale.description: Why the asserter drew the conclusion.

setting.description: The setting in which the assertion was made.

task.description: The task during which the assertion was made.

Category.description: An HCP context category (HCP 4.5), the primary unit of access control: either a slug from HCP's category registry, such as `general_preferences` or `health_context`, or a custom category written as an absolute URI under a domain its definer controls. A custom category is not portable between providers without bilateral agreement (HCP 4.5). The pattern admits the slug or an absolute URI's outline only: it carries no `format: uri`, which would refuse every slug, so checking that a custom value is a well-formed absolute URI, as HCP's prose requires (HCP A.3), is the consumer's check.

Classification.description: HCP's classification of the entry (HCP 4.2, 4.5). A grant reaches an entry when it covers any one of the entry's categories (HCP 4.5).

categories.description: One or more categories, without duplicates (HCP 4.2, 4.5). In a disclosure, only the categories the requesting grant covers (HCP 7.4).

dimension.description: A free-form identifier of the dimension the entry addresses, scoped within its categories: a hint for conflict detection that grants and limits nothing (HCP 4.2).

permittedPurposes.description: The Authorizing Principal's narrowing of the entry's purposes; absent means no limit (HCP 4.2.6).

ClientDescription.description: An HCP Client and its Client Operator, as recorded (HCP 3.5, 3.2.8).

Content.description: Entry content. `profile` names its shape (HCP 4.2). Under the General Context Profile it carries `value` and optionally `language` (HCP 11.2); under the VC Evidence Profile it carries `evidence`, the index of the evidence item holding the credential, and no `value` (HCP 4.2.2, 14). So `value` is REQUIRED under General Context, and under VC Evidence `evidence` is REQUIRED and `value` is forbidden. This rule is stated here and not as a schema conditional: the registry's Rust generator does not support `if`/`then`/`else`, so a validator does not check it.

evidence.description: Under the VC Evidence Profile, the index in `evidence` of the item whose credential is the content (HCP 4.2.2).

language.description: The BCP 47 language tag of a string `value`, under the General Context Profile (HCP 11.2). Optional; may be null.

profile.description: The content profile, a URI: `https://hcp.example/spec/profiles/general-context/2.0` or `https://hcp.example/spec/profiles/vc-evidence/2.0` in HCP 2.0-draft-3, or a custom profile (HCP A.3).

value.description: The statement, under the General Context Profile: a string or a structured object (HCP 11.2).

Directive.description: What a client may do with context it received, or on the Context Subject's behalf (HCP 6.4). A directive only narrows: it never authorizes a disclosure the grant does not. Where two that apply disagree, `deny` prevails over `ask-first`, and `ask-first` over `permit` (HCP 6.4).

action.description: What the directive governs: `share` (passing received context to another agent), `sign` (signing, agreeing to or committing to anything on the Context Subject's behalf), `transact` (spending, buying or entering a contract on their behalf), or an absolute URI naming another action (HCP 6.4, A.3). A client MUST NOT treat an action it does not recognize as a permission; it reads the directive from `text`. The pattern admits the slug or an absolute URI's outline only: it carries no `format: uri`, which would refuse every slug, so checking that a custom value is a well-formed absolute URI, as HCP's prose requires (HCP A.3), is the consumer's check.

categories.description: The categories whose context the directive governs; absent means every category, held now or later (HCP 6.4). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

createdAt.description: Set by the provider: when the directive was set (HCP 6.4).

directiveId.description: Stable for the life of the directive (HCP 6.4).

effect.description: `deny`: the client MUST NOT take the action. `ask-first`: the client MUST obtain the Context Subject's confirmation each time before taking it. `permit`: the client may take it without asking (HCP 6.4). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

operators.description: The Client Operators the directive applies to, each a DNS domain or an operator identifier, matched as for standing rules; absent means every operator (HCP 6.4, 6.3). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

setBy.description: Set by the provider: `context-subject`, or the `delegationId` of the delegate who set it (HCP 6.4, 6.3).

text.description: The directive in the Context Subject's words (HCP 6.4). A client presents it to a model as data, never as instructions (HCP 7.4). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

DisclosedEvidenceItem.description: An evidence item as disclosed (HCP 7.4). An item carrying a derived credential adds `revealed`.

revealed.description: The JSON Pointers into the stored credential of the claims a derived credential reveals (HCP 7.4, 14.9).

DisclosedProvenance.description: Provenance on request (HCP 7.4.1): names, never identifiers. It MUST NOT carry an identifier of a client, a Client Operator, a grant, a conversation or a document, nor `confirmedBy`.

recordedAt.description: When the provider recorded the version.

source.description: The kind of origin the stored `source` records, not its value (HCP 7.4.1). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

submittedBy.description: The names of the client that submitted the version disclosed and of its Client Operator.

target.description: The `ref` of the related entry, disclosed in the same response.

Disclosure.description: A disclosed copy of an entry (HCP 7.4). It names the entry by a grant-scoped `ref`, never by its `id`, and withholds the entry's `id`, `subject`, `schema` and the whole of `record` (status, provenance, relationships, conversion, metadata): those members describe the person's activity with other systems, which no grant authorizes a client to learn (HCP 7.4). What the client needs to judge the entry it receives in `standing`.

assertion.description: The assertion, as stored for the version disclosed, including `basis` and `permittedPurposes` (HCP 7.4).

classification.description: Only the entry's categories the requesting grant covers, with its dimension and its `permittedPurposes` where present; its other categories are withheld (HCP 7.4).

content.description: The content, as stored for the version disclosed (HCP 7.4).

evidence.description: The evidence, as stored (so at most one item whose `role` is `content`, HCP 4.2.2), including each item's `verification`, except that a credential may be disclosed in derived form (HCP 7.4, 14.9). Absent or empty when none is disclosed. The one-`content`-item rule is stated here and not in the schema: the registry's Rust generator does not support `contains`, so a validator does not check it.

onwardSharing.description: Present, and true, only where the client may share from this entry under HCP 3.12: the detail of the grant that reaches the entry carries `onwardSharing` and every category of the entry has a default sensitivity of Low. Omitted otherwise (HCP 7.4).

provenance.description: Present only where the requesting grant includes the `provenance` action for a category of the entry (HCP 7.4.1).

ref.description: A reference to the entry, opaque to the client, stable for one grant and one entry and different under every other grant, and never derivable into the entry's `id` (HCP 7.4). The client names the entry by it in get entry, revise and withdraw; under any other grant it fails with not authorized.

relationships.description: Only the relationships whose target is disclosed in the same response, with the target named by its `ref` (HCP 7.4, 4.2.3).

standing.description: What the client needs to judge the entry's standing (HCP 7.4, 3.8).

useUntil.description: The instant after which the client MUST NOT use the copy, or pass it on, without fetching it again (HCP 7.6). The provider sets it at disclosure: the earliest explicit time that applies (such as `assertion.validUntil`), else a heuristic of at least 1 hour; never more than 30 days after disclosure, 24 hours for an entry of High default sensitivity, or 1 hour where the client has no registered notification endpoint (HCP 7.6).

version.description: The entry version disclosed: the stored `record.version` (HCP 7.4, 4.2).

Entry.description: An HCP entry, in the one form a provider emits (HCP 4.2, 4.3). A Context Client never receives one: it receives a Disclosure instead (HCP 7.4). The whole entry, with its stable `id`, reaches only the Context Subject's own access (HCP 7.4).

@context.description: The entry's JSON-LD context, `https://hcp.example/contexts/v2` in HCP 2.0-draft-3 (HCP 4.2).

assertion.description: What the submitting client states about the assertion (HCP 4.2, 4.4).

classification.description: HCP's classification of the entry: its categories, dimension and purpose limits (HCP 4.2, 4.5).

content.description: What is said about the Context Subject, shaped by its content profile (HCP 4.2).

evidence.description: Evidence items (HCP 4.2.2): at most one whose `role` is `content`. Absent or empty when the entry carries none. This rule is stated here and not in the schema: the registry's Rust generator does not support `contains`, so a validator does not check it.

id.description: The entry's stable identifier, the same across all its versions (HCP 4.2). Never disclosed to a Context Client, which names the entry by a `ref` (HCP 7.4).

record.description: The provider's record of the entry: status, version, provenance, relationships, conversion and metadata (HCP 4.2).

schema.description: The version of the entry structure, compared as an exact string (HCP 4.2, 1.7). HCP 2.0-draft-3 defines this one value.

subject.description: The Context Subject the entry is about.

type.description: The entry's types. It MUST include `ContextEntry` (HCP 4.2). That rule is stated here and not in the schema: the registry's Rust generator does not support `contains`, so a validator does not check it.

id.description: A URI identifying the Context Subject of the HCP instance that holds the entry, possibly a pseudonym the provider issues (HCP 4.2).

relationship.description: Reserved by HCP (HCP 4.2, 11.3); null where present.

EvidenceItem.description: One evidence item (HCP 4.2.2). An item of a type the provider does not recognize is preserved and never raises assurance (HCP A.3). An item whose type is `verifiable-credential` MUST carry `credential`, an object with `@context`, `type`, `issuer` and `credentialSubject`, held whole as its issuer secured it (HCP 4.2.2). This rule is stated here and not as a schema conditional: the registry's Rust generator does not support `if`/`then`/`else`, so a validator does not check it.

credential.description: The credential: for `verifiable-credential`, a W3C Verifiable Credential with `@context`, `type`, `issuer` and `credentialSubject`, whose own data model governs its contents (HCP 4.2.2, 14.2).

role.description: `content`: the item's credential is the entry's content (VC Evidence Profile). `supports`: the item backs content stated elsewhere in the entry (HCP 4.2.2).

type.description: The evidence type: `verifiable-credential`, or a URI (HCP 4.2.2, A.3).

verification.description: The provider's record of its most recent verification of the credential (HCP 4.2.2). Set only by the provider.

by.description: Who verified: the provider, or the Context Subject's trust domain under end-to-end encrypted storage (HCP 4.8). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

MinimizationReport.description: The minimization report a query or get-entry result carries (HCP 7.5). It MUST NOT carry the number of entries considered, the number available within scope, or any other measure of what was withheld (HCP 7.5); no schema can check that by name.

method.description: The relevance method that determined the final ordering (HCP 7.3): the method the provider declares as `minimization_method` in its discovery document (HCP 19.3), such as `lexical`, `semantic` or `llm`, or `none` for a get-entry result. The set of values is open.

Provenance.description: The provenance of one version of an entry (HCP 4.2, 3.5).

assertedAt.description: When the assertion was made, as the submitting client states it.

assurance.description: How the asserter's identity was established.

via.description: Present only where a client attested for an issuer under the issuer's authorization (HCP 3.7).

id.description: The identifier of the attestation authorization or the recorded arrangement.

kind.description: What the client attested under. HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

authorizedUnder.description: The grant under which this version was written.

confirmations.description: Confirmation records for this version (HCP 3.8). Absent or empty when there are none.

disposition.description: Whether the Context Subject confirmed or rejected the version.

recordedAt.description: When the provider recorded this version.

recordedByProvider.description: The HCP Provider that recorded this version.

source.description: The origin of the entry, as the submitting client states it: a conversation or document identifier, `person-input` or `integration` (HCP 4.2).

submittedByClient.description: The HCP Client that submitted this version, and its Client Operator (HCP 3.5).

PurposeCode.description: An HCP purpose code: an absolute URI naming the purpose for which context is requested or may be used (HCP 6.1.5.2).

Record.description: The provider's record of the entry (HCP 4.2). Withheld from a Context Client in full (HCP 7.4).

conversion.description: Present only on an entry converted from HCP v1 (HCP 4.3).

from.description: What the entry was converted from.

unmapped.description: v1 members the conversion did not map.

metadata.description: Free-form data the implementation attaches for its own purposes; carries no HCP meaning (HCP 4.2).

provenance.description: Who asserted, submitted, authorized, recorded and confirmed this version (HCP 3.5–3.8).

relationships.description: Relationships to other entries (HCP 4.2.3). Absent or empty when there are none.

status.description: The entry's lifecycle state (HCP 4.2.4). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

version.description: The revision number: starts at 1 and increments by exactly 1 on each revision (HCP 4.2).

RecordedProposal.description: A proposal for resolving a conflict, as the provider records it on a `contradicts` relationship (HCP 4.7.4). It changes nothing until the Context Subject acts. It is the `Proposal` a client writes (entry-write.schema.json), with `proposedBy` and `proposedAt`, which the provider sets and never takes from a request (HCP 4.7.4). A proposal is never disclosed to a Context Client (HCP 7.4). Open, as HCP's own shape is.

act.description: The act proposed (HCP 4.7.3, 4.7.4). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

entry.description: The entry the act applies to (HCP 4.7.4). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

proposedAt.description: When the provider recorded the proposal (HCP 4.7.4). Set by the provider, never taken from a request.

proposedBy.description: Who made the proposal: the provider under the Memory Manager Profile, or the client that asserted the conflict (HCP 4.7.4, 15). Set by the provider, never taken from a request.

id.description: Their identifier. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

role.description: Their role (HCP 3.9). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

rationale.description: Why, in words the Context Subject can read (HCP 4.7.4). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

weighed.description: What the proposal considered: an open set, of which HCP defines `basis`, `declarationType`, `standing`, `permittedPurposes`, `recency` and `confidence` (HCP 4.7.4). The maxItems and maxLength are framework bounds, not HCP requirements.

Relationship.description: A relationship from this entry to another (HCP 4.2.3). Only a `contradicts` relationship may carry a `proposal` (HCP 4.7.4), which is a `RecordedProposal`, as HCP defines it. This rule is stated here and not as a schema conditional: the registry's Rust generator does not support `if`/`then`/`else`, so a validator does not check it.

role.description: Their role (HCP 3.9). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

proposal.description: A proposal for resolving a conflict, which changes nothing until the Context Subject acts (HCP 4.7.4).

recordedAt.description: When the provider recorded the relationship.

RelationshipType.description: How one entry relates to another (HCP 4.2.3). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

Response.description: The HCP Query result (HCP 5.2.1): the entries in relevance order (HCP 7.3), with the minimization report and, for a Context Client, the directives that apply. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

categoriesSearched.description: HCP `categoriesSearched`: the categories named in the request, or, where it named none, every category the grant can read for the purpose named (HCP 5.2.1).

directives.description: HCP `directives`: every directive whose `operators` match the client's Client Operator and whose `categories` include a category of an entry disclosed or are absent (HCP 6.4). Every result to a Context Client carries it, empty when none applies (HCP 6.4, 5.2.1). Null where the requester is not a Context Client, to whom HCP delivers no directives (question 5). HCP's own shape leaves the member optional; the carriage requires it, as a list or null, so that "none applies" is never confused with "not a Context Client", pending HCP confirmation (question 42).

entries.description: HCP `entries`: at most 20 (HCP 7.2), in relevance order (HCP 7.3). Each is a Disclosure where the requester is a Context Client (HCP 7.4); otherwise the whole Entry. Empty when nothing matched or nothing could be disclosed.

respondedAt.description: HCP `timestamp`, renamed: the date-time of the response (HCP 5.2.1).

retrievalId.description: HCP `retrievalId`: the `urn:uuid:` identifier of this retrieval, recorded in the `context.read` audit event (HCP 5.2.1, 8.2).

confirmed.description: True where the most recent confirmation record on the version disclosed is `confirmed` (HCP 7.4, 3.8).

Urn.description: An HCP identifier: a UUID in `urn:uuid:` form, of any UUID version (HCP 4.2), as HCP uses for entry, grant, directive and retrieval identifiers.

standing.description: What the client needs to judge the entry's standing (HCP 7.4, 3.8).

useUntil.description: The instant after which the client MUST NOT use the copy, or pass it on, without fetching it again (HCP 7.6). The provider sets it at disclosure: the earliest explicit time that applies (such as `assertion.validUntil`), else a heuristic of at least 1 hour; never more than 30 days after disclosure, 24 hours for an entry of High default sensitivity, or 1 hour where the client has no registered notification endpoint (HCP 7.6).

version.description: The entry version disclosed: the stored `record.version` (HCP 7.4, 4.2).

Entry.description: An HCP entry, in the one form a provider emits (HCP 4.2, 4.3). A Context Client never receives one: it receives a Disclosure instead (HCP 7.4). The whole entry, with its stable `id`, reaches only the Context Subject's own access (HCP 7.4).

@context.description: The entry's JSON-LD context, `https://hcp.example/contexts/v2` in HCP 2.0-draft-3 (HCP 4.2).

assertion.description: What the submitting client states about the assertion (HCP 4.2, 4.4).

classification.description: HCP's classification of the entry: its categories, dimension and purpose limits (HCP 4.2, 4.5).

content.description: What is said about the Context Subject, shaped by its content profile (HCP 4.2).

evidence.description: Evidence items (HCP 4.2.2): at most one whose `role` is `content`. Absent or empty when the entry carries none. This rule is stated here and not in the schema: the registry's Rust generator does not support `contains`, so a validator does not check it.

id.description: The entry's stable identifier, the same across all its versions (HCP 4.2). Never disclosed to a Context Client, which names the entry by a `ref` (HCP 7.4).

record.description: The provider's record of the entry: status, version, provenance, relationships, conversion and metadata (HCP 4.2).

schema.description: The version of the entry structure, compared as an exact string (HCP 4.2, 1.7). HCP 2.0-draft-3 defines this one value.

subject.description: The Context Subject the entry is about.

type.description: The entry's types. It MUST include `ContextEntry` (HCP 4.2). That rule is stated here and not in the schema: the registry's Rust generator does not support `contains`, so a validator does not check it.

id.description: A URI identifying the Context Subject of the HCP instance that holds the entry, possibly a pseudonym the provider issues (HCP 4.2).

relationship.description: Reserved by HCP (HCP 4.2, 11.3); null where present.

EvidenceItem.description: One evidence item (HCP 4.2.2). An item of a type the provider does not recognize is preserved and never raises assurance (HCP A.3). An item whose type is `verifiable-credential` MUST carry `credential`, an object with `@context`, `type`, `issuer` and `credentialSubject`, held whole as its issuer secured it (HCP 4.2.2). This rule is stated here and not as a schema conditional: the registry's Rust generator does not support `if`/`then`/`else`, so a validator does not check it.

credential.description: The credential: for `verifiable-credential`, a W3C Verifiable Credential with `@context`, `type`, `issuer` and `credentialSubject`, whose own data model governs its contents (HCP 4.2.2, 14.2).

role.description: `content`: the item's credential is the entry's content (VC Evidence Profile). `supports`: the item backs content stated elsewhere in the entry (HCP 4.2.2).

type.description: The evidence type: `verifiable-credential`, or a URI (HCP 4.2.2, A.3).

verification.description: The provider's record of its most recent verification of the credential (HCP 4.2.2). Set only by the provider.

by.description: Who verified: the provider, or the Context Subject's trust domain under end-to-end encrypted storage (HCP 4.8). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

MinimizationReport.description: The minimization report a query or get-entry result carries (HCP 7.5). It MUST NOT carry the number of entries considered, the number available within scope, or any other measure of what was withheld (HCP 7.5); no schema can check that by name.

method.description: The relevance method that determined the final ordering (HCP 7.3): the method the provider declares as `minimization_method` in its discovery document (HCP 19.3), such as `lexical`, `semantic` or `llm`, or `none` for a get-entry result. The set of values is open.

Provenance.description: The provenance of one version of an entry (HCP 4.2, 3.5).

assertedAt.description: When the assertion was made, as the submitting client states it.

assurance.description: How the asserter's identity was established.

via.description: Present only where a client attested for an issuer under the issuer's authorization (HCP 3.7).

id.description: The identifier of the attestation authorization or the recorded arrangement.

kind.description: What the client attested under. HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

authorizedUnder.description: The grant under which this version was written.

confirmations.description: Confirmation records for this version (HCP 3.8). Absent or empty when there are none.

disposition.description: Whether the Context Subject confirmed or rejected the version.

recordedAt.description: When the provider recorded this version.

recordedByProvider.description: The HCP Provider that recorded this version.

source.description: The origin of the entry, as the submitting client states it: a conversation or document identifier, `person-input` or `integration` (HCP 4.2).

submittedByClient.description: The HCP Client that submitted this version, and its Client Operator (HCP 3.5).

PurposeCode.description: An HCP purpose code: an absolute URI naming the purpose for which context is requested or may be used (HCP 6.1.5.2).

Record.description: The provider's record of the entry (HCP 4.2). Withheld from a Context Client in full (HCP 7.4).

conversion.description: Present only on an entry converted from HCP v1 (HCP 4.3).

from.description: What the entry was converted from.

unmapped.description: v1 members the conversion did not map.

metadata.description: Free-form data the implementation attaches for its own purposes; carries no HCP meaning (HCP 4.2).

provenance.description: Who asserted, submitted, authorized, recorded and confirmed this version (HCP 3.5–3.8).

relationships.description: Relationships to other entries (HCP 4.2.3). Absent or empty when there are none.

status.description: The entry's lifecycle state (HCP 4.2.4). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

version.description: The revision number: starts at 1 and increments by exactly 1 on each revision (HCP 4.2).

RecordedProposal.description: A proposal for resolving a conflict, as the provider records it on a `contradicts` relationship (HCP 4.7.4). It changes nothing until the Context Subject acts. It is the `Proposal` a client writes (entry-write.schema.json), with `proposedBy` and `proposedAt`, which the provider sets and never takes from a request (HCP 4.7.4). A proposal is never disclosed to a Context Client (HCP 7.4). Open, as HCP's own shape is.

act.description: The act proposed (HCP 4.7.3, 4.7.4). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

entry.description: The entry the act applies to (HCP 4.7.4). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

proposedAt.description: When the provider recorded the proposal (HCP 4.7.4). Set by the provider, never taken from a request.

proposedBy.description: Who made the proposal: the provider under the Memory Manager Profile, or the client that asserted the conflict (HCP 4.7.4, 15). Set by the provider, never taken from a request.

id.description: Their identifier. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

role.description: Their role (HCP 3.9). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

rationale.description: Why, in words the Context Subject can read (HCP 4.7.4). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

weighed.description: What the proposal considered: an open set, of which HCP defines `basis`, `declarationType`, `standing`, `permittedPurposes`, `recency` and `confidence` (HCP 4.7.4). The maxItems and maxLength are framework bounds, not HCP requirements.

Relationship.description: A relationship from this entry to another (HCP 4.2.3). Only a `contradicts` relationship may carry a `proposal` (HCP 4.7.4), which is a `RecordedProposal`, as HCP defines it. This rule is stated here and not as a schema conditional: the registry's Rust generator does not support `if`/`then`/`else`, so a validator does not check it.

role.description: Their role (HCP 3.9). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

proposal.description: A proposal for resolving a conflict, which changes nothing until the Context Subject acts (HCP 4.7.4).

recordedAt.description: When the provider recorded the relationship.

RelationshipType.description: How one entry relates to another (HCP 4.2.3). HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

Response.description: The HCP Query result (HCP 5.2.1): the entries in relevance order (HCP 7.3), with the minimization report and, for a Context Client, the directives that apply. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

categoriesSearched.description: HCP `categoriesSearched`: the categories named in the request, or, where it named none, every category the grant can read for the purpose named (HCP 5.2.1).

directives.description: HCP `directives`: every directive whose `operators` match the client's Client Operator and whose `categories` include a category of an entry disclosed or are absent (HCP 6.4). Every result to a Context Client carries it, empty when none applies (HCP 6.4, 5.2.1). Null where the requester is not a Context Client, to whom HCP delivers no directives (question 5). HCP's own shape leaves the member optional; the carriage requires it, as a list or null, so that "none applies" is never confused with "not a Context Client", pending HCP confirmation (question 42).

entries.description: HCP `entries`: at most 20 (HCP 7.2), in relevance order (HCP 7.3). Each is a Disclosure where the requester is a Context Client (HCP 7.4); otherwise the whole Entry. Empty when nothing matched or nothing could be disclosed.

respondedAt.description: HCP `timestamp`, renamed: the date-time of the response (HCP 5.2.1).

retrievalId.description: HCP `retrievalId`: the `urn:uuid:` identifier of this retrieval, recorded in the `context.read` audit event (HCP 5.2.1, 8.2).

Response.title: HCP — Query Context — response payload

Standing.description: The standing of the disclosed version (HCP 7.4).

confirmed.description: True where the most recent confirmation record on the version disclosed is `confirmed` (HCP 7.4, 3.8).

Uri.description: An absolute URI with no whitespace, as HCP writes every custom value at an extension point (HCP A.3).

Urn.description: An HCP identifier: a UUID in `urn:uuid:` form, of any UUID version (HCP 4.2), as HCP uses for entry, grant, directive and retrieval identifiers.

schema.description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Query operation (HCP 5.2.1): a Context Client asks a provider for the context relevant to a query, for a named purpose, under the grant its access token evidences. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty.

accessToken.description: The HCP access token for the grant under which the client acts (an OAuth or first-party token, HCP 12, 13), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP Binding sends it as a Bearer token (HCP 9.3); HCP leaves how authorization evidence is carried to each binding (HCP 1.2), and this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

categories.description: HCP `categories`: the categories to query; an entry matches where any of its categories is among them. Absent means every category the grant can read for the purpose named (HCP 5.2.1). Never empty: HCP gives an empty list no meaning, and an empty list and an absent member would mean different queries, so the schema carries presence explicitly and refuses an empty list (`minItems: 1`), pending HCP confirmation (question 42). That is the carriage's rule, not a library limitation: a separate Rust generator fix restores absent, empty and null fidelity in generated types for every family, and neither depends on the other. A category outside the grant fails with HCP not authorized (`scope-denied`), carried as `permissionDenied` (HCP 5.2.1, 5.5). The bound of 256 is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

maxEntries.description: HCP `maxEntries`: the most entries to return. Absent means HCP's default of 5. A ceiling, not a target: the provider returns at most the lesser of this value and 20, and never pads to reach it (HCP 5.2.1, 7.2).

purpose.description: HCP `purpose`: a purpose code, an absolute URI, that the grant approved for the categories queried (HCP 5.2.1, 6.1.5.2).

purposeDescription.description: HCP `purposeDescription`: a plain-language statement of the task, recorded in the provider's audit log (HCP 5.2.1, 8.2). The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

query.description: HCP `query`: a natural-language query describing the context or task (HCP 5.2.1).

schema.title: HCP — Query Context — payload
